title: Senior Sales Manager at Super Micro Computer Inc. Sees Supply-Chain Reliability Driving AI Server Cooling Choices
expert: Senior sales manager selling L10/L11 AI racks at Super Micro Computer (current)
verdict: A Supermicro rack sales manager sees AVC cold plates, manifolds and CDUs in liquid-cooled builds but calls cooling a \$20,000 'tax' on a \$9 million rack, so availability, not brand, picks the supplier.

Nvidia content and share: 🔴 Auras cold-plate share roughly 4% to over 10% after joining the GB300 AVL (hearsay), at the top of the ex-AVC account manager's Auras 5–10% (SB #64467): share leaking. → Tenet 1 (Nvidia content and share) ↓
🔴 Server OEMs insourcing cold plates, CDUs and quick disconnects, keeping third parties as at least one alternative; first read on OEM insourcing. → Tenet 1 (Nvidia content and share) ↓
🟢 GB200, GB300, Vera Rubin and MI350X deployments all liquid-cooled (first-hand), consistent with mgmt's >50% liquid penetration in 2027 (SB #65392).
Gross margin: 🔴 Cooling 'a couple thousand dollars' vs \$50,000–\$100,000 per GPU; low differentiation, vs JPM's AVC ASP raises on switch trays (SB #58857): no pricing power seen from the rack side. → Tenet 3 (GM 34%+) ↓
🔴 Nvidia designs GB300/Vera Rubin racks and may supply cold plates with compute trays, limiting supplier leverage; first read. → Tenet 3 (GM 34%+) ↓
ASIC liquid-cooling start: 🟡 Only the top five hyperscalers can fund custom ASIC boards; other customers stay on Intel/AMD, first read. → Tenet 2 (ASIC ramp) →

changes: Auras cold-plate share roughly 4% to over 10% (hearsay) vs ex-AVC account manager's Auras 5–10% on GB series (SB #64467, 2026-09-20): Auras gaining.
Cooling a couple thousand dollars per GPU tray vs JPM's VR cold-plate content US\$3.0–3.5k per tray (SB #58854): similar order of magnitude.
Cooling lead times 'definitely increased' over the past year (no weeks given); first read on cooling lead times, no earlier expert call or stored row.
Rack-level cost up roughly 10% y/y, driven by memory (+10–20% m/m); first read on rack cost; no earlier expert call or stored row.
thesis_impact: Tenet 1 (Nvidia content and share): ↓ — Auras share 4% to over 10% (hearsay) and OEMs insourcing cold plates and CDUs.
Tenet 2 (ASIC ramp): → — only the top five hyperscalers build custom ASIC boards; no AVC-specific ASIC figure.
Tenet 3 (Margin and EPS): ↓ — cooling a \$20,000 'tax' on a \$9 million rack and Nvidia-set designs limit supplier pricing.
